title: The long way back, i
logline: The strip tries being a travelogue. Wood drives to Coos Bay. The strip pretends it was far.

panels.composition: The Datsun on 101, south, morning. A hand-lettered caption in a travelogue voice.
panels.caption: DAY ONE. We leave Small Wood at dawn. The road south is the road I have never taken far enough.

image.prompt: an old Datsun driving south on a coastal highway at dawn with a young man at the wheel and a dog in the passenger seat, muddy digital flats, a caption box

panels.composition: A sign: COOS BAY 61. The dog looking at it. The caption undeterred.
panels.caption: The country changes. The spruce give way to — different spruce.

image.prompt: a road sign reading COOS BAY 61 seen through a windshield, a small dog looking at it

panels.composition: A diner in Coos Bay. Wood drawing the diner. It looks like the one in Small Wood. The caption knows.
panels.caption: DAY ONE, NOON. A diner. I draw it. It is, in every respect that matters, the diner at home. This is the travelogue's first discovery.

image.prompt: a young man drawing in a diner booth with a dog under the table, the diner ordinary, a caption box

panels.composition: The Datsun, north, evening. Home by dark. The caption, smaller.
panels.caption: DAY ONE, DUSK. We return. The long way back was sixty-one miles. — to be continued

image.prompt: an old Datsun driving north on a coastal highway at dusk, small, a caption box, no dialogue

art.palette: limited; Sundays in watercolor, good now
art.paper: bristol; the browser; from 2008 coastal newsprint a week behind

notes: The travelogue. Sixty-one miles. 'To be continued' — it continues for six weeks and never gets farther than Florence.
